extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples. Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline using LLM inspectors, then human review ensures each curated sample exhibits visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requires advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.publisher: University of Science and Technology of China; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shanghai AI Laboratory
extraction.citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv preprint arXiv:2403.20330.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMBench, SEED-Bench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista. The collection process involved two steps: (1) an automated coarse filter pipeline using 8 LLM inspectors (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, and six open-source LLMs sized 20B+) with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to filter out samples that could be answered without visual content or that were leaked; (2) manual review by three experts to ensure visual dependency, capability coverage, and advanced multi-modal reasoning requirements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples collected from six source benchmarks: MMBench (MMBench-EN-Dev), SEED-Bench (SEED-Image), MMMU (MMMU-Val), ScienceQA (ScienceQA-Test), AI2D (AI2D-Test), and MathVista (MathVista-Mini). Initial pool of 22,401 samples was reduced to 11,607 candidates after coarse filtering, and finally to 1,500 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated coarse filtering pipeline: samples were evaluated using 8 LLM inspectors (2 closed-source: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; 6 open-source: InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B) with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Hit counts were recorded for each sample, and only samples with hit counts of two or fewer (i.e., around 75% of LLM inspectors failed to provide correct answer without visual input) were retained. All questions were converted into multiple-choice format. Heuristic matching rules were developed to calculate accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: (1) each sample's answer should be based on understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Samples were categorized along 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Samples were categorized into four difficulty levels based on hit counts of 16 LVLMs: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11 hits), hard (4-7 hits), and tough (0-3 hits). Each of the 6 core capability dimensions contains a balanced 250 samples, with relatively even distribution across the 18 detailed axes.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B (used as LLM inspectors); 16 LVLMs including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series (used for difficulty assessment); VLMEvalKit codebase
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM's and LVLM's training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark addresses fairness and reliability in evaluating LVLMs by ensuring visual dependency and minimizing data leakage, helping prevent misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and avoiding misleading the study of LVLM development.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Samples are sourced primarily from SEED-Bench (28.3%), MMBench (24.4%), MathVista (23.0%), AI2D (13.1%), MMMU (6.7%), and ScienceQA (4.6%), which may reflect biases inherent in these source benchmarks. The benchmark focuses on English-language evaluation samples.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark consists of only 1,500 samples, which is relatively small. It is a static test set that may be vulnerable to future data leakage as LVLMs continue to train on more data. The authors acknowledge the need for dynamic evaluation methods in future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to assess their actual multi-modal capabilities across 6 core dimensions: Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, and Mathematics. Also used with multi-modal gain (MG) and multi-modal leakage (ML) metrics to probe LVLMs' actual performance gains and data leakage from multi-modal training.
